title: disk
body:
## disk

Creates a flat circular disk as one polygon whose segments vertices lie on a circle of the given radius in the local XY plane, centred on centre, with its normal along +Z. The polygon is inscribed in the circle, so its area is slightly smaller than pi r squared at low segment counts. Use it for end plates, markers and backdrops; use grid or subdivision when the face needs interior vertices.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The single n-gon has no interior vertices, so deforming it with bend or twist has little effect.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `disk`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Radius of the circle on which the disk's boundary vertices lie. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `1` |
| `segments` | Number of boundary vertices of the single polygon; more segments approximate the circle more closely. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `32` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the disk's centre. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated disk is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
